sentence.ja: 毎朝[まいあさ]八時[はちじ]に{学校[がっこう]}へ行[い]きます。
sentence.en: I go to school at eight every morning.

mnemonic.story: Gaku is the "study" in daigaku; kō is the second half of kōkō, high school. A study-place is a **school**, where everyone *gawks* at one *coat* left on a hook. Gakkō.

sentence.ja: 妹[いもうと]は{高校[こうこう]}一年生[いちねんせい]です。
sentence.en: My younger sister is a first-year in high school.

mnemonic.story: On the first day of **high school** everyone hangs a *coat* on the same hook, *coat* on *coat*, until the hook snaps with a crack. Kō-kō: high school, both vowels long.

sentence.ja: 田中[たなか]さんは{大学[だいがく]}の先生[せんせい]です。
sentence.en: Tanaka-san is a university professor.

mnemonic.story: Outside the **university** gates, graduates *dye* their gowns purple in a bubbling vat while tourists stop to *gawk*, splashes staining the cobbles. Dai-gaku: university, college.

sentence.ja: ケンさんは{学生[がくせい]}ですか。
sentence.en: Is Ken a student?

mnemonic.story: The whole lecture hall turns to *gawk* as one **student** climbs onto her chair to *say* the answer, chalk dust drifting in the light. Gaku-sei: student.

sentence.ja: 弟[おとうと]は{高校生[こうこうせい]}です。
sentence.en: My younger brother is in high school.

mnemonic.story: Kōkō is high school, sei is student: a **high school student**. The two coats from kōkō now have a teenager inside, ready to *say* her name at roll call. Kōkō-sei.

sentence.ja: 山田[やまだ]さんは{大学生[だいがくせい]}ですか。
sentence.en: Is Yamada-san a college student?

mnemonic.story: Daigaku is university, and sei is the *say* from gakusei, a student: a **college student**. Picture one saying her name at the purple-dyed gates on day one. Daigaku-sei.

sentence.ja: ケンさんは{留学生[りゅうがくせい]}です。
sentence.en: Ken is an international student.

mnemonic.story: At passport control the officer squints at your backpack: "*Are you* gakusei?" Slur it, r'you-gakusei, and you're an **international student**, a student from abroad. Ryū-gakusei.

sentence.ja: 山田[やまだ]さんは英語[えいご]の{先生[せんせい]}です。
sentence.en: Yamada-san is an English teacher.

mnemonic.story: Your **teacher** drops a *cent* into a jar each time someone can *say* the answer, coins clinking all lesson long. Sen-sei: teacher, and after a name, Professor.

sentence.ja: 明日[あした]は九時[くじ]から{授業[じゅぎょう]}があります。
sentence.en: Tomorrow I have class from nine.

mnemonic.story: You sneak *juice* and *gyoza* into **class** under your desk, and the garlic smell gives you away by the second slide. Jugyō: class.

sentence.ja: 今日[きょう]は{宿題[しゅくだい]}がたくさんあります。
sentence.en: I have a lot of homework today.

mnemonic.story: You *shook* a bottle of purple *dye* too hard, and now every page of your **homework** is dripping and violet. Shuku-dai: homework.

sentence.ja: 明日[あした]は日本語[にほんご]の{テスト}です。
sentence.en: Tomorrow is the Japanese test.

mnemonic.story: *Test* gains a final o: te-su-to, with the su whispered so it still sounds close to "test-o". **Test**.

sentence.ja: 明日[あした]は日本語[にほんご]の{試験[しけん]}があります。
sentence.en: I have a Japanese exam tomorrow.

mnemonic.story: The **exam** papers slap down on every desk, and the girl beside you whispers *she can*, *she can* to herself, pencil trembling, the clock ticking loud. Shiken: exam.

sentence.ja: {教科書[きょうかしょ]}の二十[にじゅっ]ページを読[よ]んでください。
sentence.en: Please read page twenty of the textbook.

mnemonic.story: At a *Kyoto car show*, a fat **textbook** is chained to every bumper, and you must read a whole chapter before the guard lets you sit behind the wheel. Kyō-ka-sho: textbook.

sentence.ja: 英語[えいご]の{辞書[じしょ]}はどこですか。
sentence.en: Where is the English dictionary?

mnemonic.story: "*Gee, show* me!" your friend begs, and you heave open the giant **dictionary**, pages thudding over one by one. Jisho: dictionary.

sentence.ja: この{漢字[かんじ]}を読[よ]んでください。
sentence.en: Please read this kanji.

mnemonic.story: You stir a bowl of rice *congee* and the grains drift into a perfect **Chinese character**, every brush stroke drawn in steaming porridge. Kan-ji: kanji, a Chinese character.

sentence.ja: この{単語[たんご]}が分[わ]かりません。
sentence.en: I don't understand this word.

mnemonic.story: You dance a *tango* across a giant flashcard, and every stamp of your heel prints a new **word** into the floor, click, clack. Tan-go: word, vocabulary.

sentence.ja: 日本語[にほんご]の{文法[ぶんぽう]}はあまり難[むずか]しくないです。
sentence.en: Japanese grammar isn't very hard.

mnemonic.story: Every **grammar** mistake in your essay is a speed *bump*: *oh!*, your teeth rattle, and the red pen keeps going. Bunpō, said bum-pō: grammar.

sentence.ja: さくらさんは英語[えいご]の{発音[はつおん]}がとても上手[じょうず]です。
sentence.en: Sakura's English pronunciation is really good.

mnemonic.story: The teacher makes you drill vowels with three *hats on*, so your **pronunciation** has to be loud and clear to get through the felt. Hatsu-on: pronunciation.

sentence.ja: この漢字[かんじ]の{意味[いみ]}は何[なん]ですか。
sentence.en: What does this kanji mean?

mnemonic.story: Stuck on a word's **meaning**, you run a finger down the dictionary going "*eeny, meeny*..." and pick one at random. Imi: meaning.

sentence.ja: 先生[せんせい]に{質問[しつもん]}があります。
sentence.en: I have a question for the teacher.

mnemonic.story: *She sues Mon*day in court, and the judge leans in with one **question**: "What did Monday ever do to you?" Shitsu-mon: question.

sentence.ja: この質問[しつもん]の{答[こた]え}が分[わ]かりません。
sentence.en: I don't know the answer to this question.

mnemonic.story: You flash open your *coat*, "*Ah, eh*...", and every **answer** to the test is pinned inside the lining, rustling. Kotae: answer.

sentence.ja: 宿題[しゅくだい]は教科書[きょうかしょ]の{練習[れんしゅう]}です。
sentence.en: The homework is the exercises in the textbook.

mnemonic.story: A *wren* hops into your *shoe* every morning to do its **exercises**: flap, hop, flap, again. Ren-shū: exercise, practice, as in renshū suru.

sentence.ja: 週末[しゅうまつ]に{作文[さくぶん]}を書[か]きました。
sentence.en: I wrote an essay over the weekend.

mnemonic.story: Your twelve-page **essay** won't fit in any folder, so you cram it into a paper *sack*, which bursts with a *boom*, pages snowing over the classroom. Saku-bun: essay.

sentence.ja: 田中[たなか]さんは毎朝[まいあさ]新聞[しんぶん]を{読[よ]みます}。
sentence.en: Tanaka-san reads the newspaper every morning.

mnemonic.story: A cow in tiny glasses **reads** the farm paper aloud: "*Yo*, listen to this... *moo*." She turns the page with her nose. Yom-u: to read.

sentence.ja: 友達[ともだち]に手紙[てがみ]を{書[か]きました}。
sentence.en: I wrote a letter to my friend.

mnemonic.story: You **write** a letter with a black crow's quill, and the crow on your shoulder reads along: "*Caw, coo*." Ka-ku: to write.

sentence.ja: 日本語[にほんご]で{話[はな]しません}か。
sentence.en: Shall we talk in Japanese?

mnemonic.story: Your parrot finally learns to **speak**, but it answers every question with "*Hah! Nah.*", flapping its wings on each word. Hanas-u: to speak.

sentence.ja: 山田[やまだ]さんに電話[でんわ]番号[ばんごう]を{聞[き]きます}。
sentence.en: I'll ask Yamada-san for their phone number.

breakdown.baseEn: to ask, to listen, to hear

mnemonic.story: You press your ear to the *key*hole and **listen**: a *cook* inside is humming and chopping onions. Kik-u: to listen, and with に, to ask.

sentence.ja: 田中[たなか]さんは英語[えいご]が{わかります}。
sentence.en: Tanaka-san understands English.

mnemonic.story: Your cousin tosses fried rice in a *wok* and it finally clicks: "*Ah!*" Now you **understand**. Waka-ru: to understand; the thing you understand takes ga.

sentence.ja: 毎週[まいしゅう]ピアノを{習[なら]っています}。
sentence.en: I take piano lessons every week.

mnemonic.story: In *Nara*, a bowing deer teaches you to bow back. You **learn** fast, because each sloppy bow earns a headbutt: *ow*! Nara-u: to learn, from a teacher.

sentence.ja: 土曜日[どようび]に子供[こども]に英語[えいご]を{教[おし]えます}。
sentence.en: I teach English to kids on Saturdays.

mnemonic.story: You **teach** a parrot to watch the class, and whenever a student misspells a word it squawks "*Oh, she errs!*" and taps the board with its beak. Oshie-ru: to teach.

sentence.ja: 漢字[かんじ]をたくさん{覚[おぼ]えました}。
sentence.en: I memorized a lot of kanji.

mnemonic.story: You **memorize** a whole symphony by playing it on an *oboe*, note by reedy note, until your lips buzz and you could play it asleep. Oboe-ru: to memorize.

sentence.ja: 先生[せんせい]、宿題[しゅくだい]を{忘[わす]れました}。
sentence.en: Sensei, I forgot my homework.

mnemonic.story: At a party you **forget** a guest's name and stammer "*What's-her*-name..." while she taps her foot, ice clinking in her glass. Wasure-ru: to forget; also to leave something behind.

sentence.ja: 週末[しゅうまつ]も{勉強[べんきょう]します}。
sentence.en: I study on weekends too.

mnemonic.story: On a stone *bench* in *Kyoto* you **study** until the temple lamps come on, flashcards flapping in the wind. Benkyō plus suru, to do: to study.

sentence.ja: 毎晩[まいばん]ギターを{練習[れんしゅう]しています}。
sentence.en: I practice the guitar every night.

mnemonic.story: A tiny *wren* **practices** tap dancing inside your *shoe*, tick-tick-tick, all night long on the closet floor. Renshū suru: to practice.

sentence.ja: 兄[あに]はアメリカに{留学[りゅうがく]しました}。
sentence.en: My older brother studied abroad in America.

mnemonic.story: A ryūgakusei is an international student, and gaku is the study you *gawk* at in a foreign classroom. Swap sei for suru and you're doing it: **studying abroad**. Ryūgaku suru.

sentence.ja: 休[やす]みに{国[くに]}へ帰[かえ]ります。
sentence.en: I'm going back to my home country for the break.

mnemonic.story: A homing pigeon lands on your *knee* and *coos*, a tiny flag of its home **country** tied to one leg. Kuni: country, or the place you come from.

sentence.ja: {外国[がいこく]}に行[い]ったことがありますか。
sentence.en: Have you ever been to a foreign country?

mnemonic.story: A *guy* in sunglasses cracks open a *coke* in every **foreign country** he lands in, and it fizzes all over his passport stamps. Gai-koku: foreign country.

sentence.ja: {日本[にほん]}は今[いま]、夜[よる]です。
sentence.en: It's night in Japan right now.

mnemonic.story: Down on one *knee*, a swordsmith *hones* a blade until it sings, sparks hissing onto the tatami: **Japan**. Ni-hon. Nippon is the same name said with more force.

sentence.ja: 山田[やまだ]さんは{日本人[にほんじん]}ですか。
sentence.en: Is Yamada-san Japanese?

mnemonic.story: Nihon is Japan and jin is a person: **Japanese people**, or one Japanese person. Picture a Tokyo commuter in pressed *jeans*, a tiny red sun stitched on one knee. Nihon-jin.

sentence.ja: {日本語[にほんご]}の先生[せんせい]は田中[たなか]さんです。
sentence.en: Our Japanese teacher is Tanaka-san.

mnemonic.story: Nihon is Japan and go is language: the **Japanese language**. The swordsmith looks up from his whetstone and barks "*Go!*" at his apprentice, in Japanese of course. Nihon-go.

sentence.ja: {英語[えいご]}の先生[せんせい]はアメリカ人[じん]です。
sentence.en: The English teacher is American.

mnemonic.story: Go is language, as in nihongo. Ei sounds like the letter *A*, the first letter of the alphabet English is written in. A + go: **English**. Ei-go: English.

sentence.ja: 田中[たなか]さんの友達[ともだち]は{アメリカ}人[じん]です。
sentence.en: Tanaka-san's friend is American.

mnemonic.story: *America* keeps four even beats, a-me-ri-ka, the r a quick tap of the tongue. It means the **U.S.A.** in particular, not the Americas as a whole.

sentence.ja: {カナダ}は今[いま]、午後[ごご]五時[ごじ]です。
sentence.en: It's 5 p.m. in Canada now.

mnemonic.story: *Canada* stays at three beats, ka-na-da, but flat and even, with no stress on the first. **Canada**.

sentence.ja: 山田[やまだ]さんのお母[かあ]さんは{イギリス}人[じん]です。
sentence.en: Yamada-san's mother is British.

mnemonic.story: Borrowed centuries ago from Portuguese *Inglês*, "English", and reshaped as i-gi-ri-su. It means **Britain**, and people use it loosely for England too.

sentence.ja: {オーストラリア}の大学[だいがく]の学生[がくせい]です。
sentence.en: I'm a student at an Australian university.

mnemonic.story: *Australia* stretches to six beats, ō-su-to-ra-ri-a: a long ō up front and a vowel after every consonant. **Australia**.

sentence.ja: 田中[たなか]さんの専攻[せんこう]は{中国[ちゅうごく]}の歴史[れきし]です。
sentence.en: Tanaka-san's major is Chinese history.

mnemonic.story: In **China** a chef hands you one dumpling: *chew* it, then *go cook* the next batch yourself, steam hissing out of the bamboo basket. Chū-goku: China.

sentence.ja: ケンさんの友達[ともだち]は{韓国[かんこく]}の留学生[りゅうがくせい]です。
sentence.en: Ken's friend is an international student from Korea.

mnemonic.story: In **Korea** your host proves she *can cook*: meat sizzles on the table grill and kimchi steam fogs up your glasses. Kan-koku: Korea.

sentence.ja: 今週[こんしゅう]は{仕事[しごと]}が忙[いそが]しいです。
sentence.en: Work is busy this week.

mnemonic.story: "*She go to* **work**?" your toddler asks, pointing as your sister sprints for the bus, briefcase flapping and toast still in her mouth. Shigoto: job, work.

sentence.ja: 兄[あに]の{会社[かいしゃ]}は東京[とうきょう]にあります。
sentence.en: My older brother's company is in Tokyo.

mnemonic.story: A *kite* tugs at the roof of the **company** building, and on the other end of the string a *shah* in silk robes runs board meetings from up there. Kai-sha: company.

sentence.ja: 山田[やまだ]さんは{会社員[かいしゃいん]}です。
sentence.en: Yamada-san is an office worker.

mnemonic.story: On lunch break an **office worker** flies a *kite* off the roof, and it tangles in the sign of the *Shah*'s *Inn* next door. Kaisha (company) + in (member): kaisha-in.

sentence.ja: うちの{社長[しゃちょう]}は毎日[まいにち]七時[しちじ]に会社[かいしゃ]に来[き]ます。
sentence.en: Our company president gets to the office at seven every day.

mnemonic.story: The board crowns a *shah*, *chosen* by a show of hands, and seats him in the gold chair on the top floor: **company president**. Sha-chō: president of a company.

sentence.ja: コンビニで{アルバイト}をします。
sentence.en: I work part-time at a convenience store.

mnemonic.story: From the German *Arbeit*, "work": a-ru-ba-i-to. In Japan it narrowed to a student's **part-time job**, and friends shorten it to baito.

sentence.ja: さくらさんは{医者[いしゃ]}です。
sentence.en: Sakura is a doctor.

mnemonic.story: "Say *eee*," the **doctor** tells the *shah*, peering down the royal throat over a cold wooden stick. I-sha: doctor.

sentence.ja: さくらさんのお姉[ねえ]さんは{看護師[かんごし]}です。
sentence.en: Sakura's older sister is a nurse.

mnemonic.story: "*Can go?*" you ask, one leg out of bed. "No," says *she*, the **nurse**, tucking you back under a starchy sheet. Kan-go-shi: nurse.

sentence.ja: ケンさんのお父[とう]さんは{弁護士[べんごし]}です。
sentence.en: Ken's father is a lawyer.

mnemonic.story: The **lawyer** slaps the missing receipt on the table, "*Bingo!*", and *she* wins the case. Ben-go-shi: lawyer. Kangoshi, the nurse, differs only in its first beat.

sentence.ja: 駅[えき]の前[まえ]に{警察官[けいさつかん]}がいます。
sentence.en: There's a police officer in front of the station.

mnemonic.story: A **police officer** opens an evidence *case* and finds a *satsuma* jammed inside a soda *can*: very suspicious. Keisatsu-kan: police officer.

sentence.ja: 私[わたし]は{歌手[かしゅ]}になりたいです。
sentence.en: I want to become a singer.

mnemonic.story: A **singer** gargles a handful of salted *cashews* before every show, and her high note comes out rich and buttery. Kashu: singer.

sentence.ja: 好[す]きな{作家[さっか]}はだれですか。
sentence.en: Who's your favorite writer?

mnemonic.story: A **writer** kicks a *soccer* ball against her study wall, thud, thud, until the next line comes. Keep it short, sakka, for writer; stretch the end, sakkā, and it's soccer.

sentence.ja: 姉[あね]は東京[とうきょう]の病院[びょういん]で{働[はたら]いています}。
sentence.en: My older sister works at a hospital in Tokyo.

mnemonic.story: You **work** all day on a road crew, dragging a *hot tar rake* through steaming black goo that sticks to your boots. Hatarak-u: to work.
